Default disposition of tester mail is DISCARD: a helper discard_mail() on the tester marks every personal envelope to 'tester' delivered and keeps nothing; called at the end of every cairn test run. A keep is a named choice in code, never the default.

The standing undelivered pile addressed to the tester is drained ONCE by a scratchpad script (the bus store is instance-space, not a record of truth); the count drained goes on the verdict artifact. After the build the next pile is the tester's job.

The press_office FOLDER (~/.cairn/folders/press_office — instanceizer tenant, no device, no charter) is OWNED by the cairn device: cairn's charter owns[] += that folder, through the artifact door's charter verb, recompile_gate.sh poked in the same act. Its recorder is ALREADY fed from the email by the bus (bus.py:208 _try_folder_delivery, 167 records) — nothing new activates it; the one undelivered press_office WATCHME envelope is diagnosed at build (first hypothesis: the cached None at bus.py:225 never retries a failed load) and fixed there with one tooth.
A reply carrying refused[] is printed by the tester at the exchange (one line per refused seal with its reason) — never stored silently.
IOU, named not built: the tester watching for a SPECIFIC email as part of a test. When it comes, it is a keep choice in discard_mail(), not a new channel.

SUPERSEDES D1, D2 and D3's owner — applies answered question open-9d1bb9b4d708, Akien 2026-09-23 verbatim: 'All mail generated by tester has to be managed by the testers shim. Period.' and '...they are of no use once the testing is complete. And that they can safely be thrown away.' The taking lives in TesterShim (cairn/devices/tester/shim.py), never in the CLI: no discard_mail() helper, no read-after-post in cli.py.

THE SHIM DISPOSES. TesterShim overrides deliver(envelope): an envelope whose reply_to is non-empty (an answer to something the tester sent) is disposed in the shim and nothing is kept — for each entry of body.refused it prints one line '  refused: <ticket> — <reason>' to stdout (D5), for each entry of body.crossed '  crossed: <ticket>', emits one 'reply_disposed' event (values: reply_to, sender, crossed count, refused count), and returns {'disposed': True, 'reply_to': <id>}. Every envelope with no reply_to goes to super().deliver(envelope) unchanged (bounces, verbs and probe findings keep their paths). BaseShim._check_mail writes the receipt after deliver returns (cairn/tools/base/shim.py, record_delivery by=self.device_id), so the shim's take IS the receipt; nothing else receipts tester mail.

THE EXCHANGE WIRES THE TESTER. In cairn/devices/tester/cli.py the seal announcement's reach becomes reach('codemother', 'harbor_master', 'tester'), so codemother's reply — posted inside post()'s poke chain — is delivered synchronously to TesterShim in this same process. One exchange, no poll, no second process (D1's constraint kept). Nothing else in that block changes; bus.flush() still follows the posts.

THE ONE-TIME DRAIN GOES THROUGH THE SHIM. Measured 2026-10-02 (BusDevice().undelivered): 480 codemother->tester 'sealed reply' envelopes, 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-02. After the build commit CC runs a scratchpad script that does reach('tester') and calls the tester shim's own _check_mail() until undelivered(to='tester') is 0, reading the count before and after; the count goes on the verdict. The drain is the tester disposing its own mail, invoked once by hand — falsifier (5) as written.
